citations.quote: Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty, there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

For $0<\gamma<1$, a data-indexed set rule $C_n:\mathsf Y_n\to\mathcal P(\Theta)$ is a posterior credible set at level $1-\gamma$ if its membership graph $\{(y,\theta):\theta\in C_n(y)\}$ is in $\mathcal Y_n\otimes\mathcal T$ and $\Pi_n(C_n(y)\mid y)\ge1-\gamma$ for every $y$ in its declared data domain.

Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$.

derivations.claim: The positive symmetric normalized standard-normal density makes its CDF continuous and strictly increasing, with value 1/2 at zero and limit one at infinity; the intermediate value theorem gives a unique positive z with Phi(z)=0.975.
Multiplying the N(0,1) prior density by the N(theta,1) likelihood and completing the square gives the normalized posterior N(Y/2,1/2).
At the fixed truth theta*=2r+1, with Y=theta*+Z, interval membership is equivalent to 1<=Z<=4r+1.
The interval membership graph is closed as the inverse image of [-r,r] under a continuous map, hence Borel, and the fixed-truth membership event is measurable.
Under the posterior N(Y/2,1/2), the central interval of radius z/sqrt(2) has mass Phi(z)-Phi(-z)=0.95 for every Y.
The event 1<=Z<=4r+1 has probability strictly less than P(Z>=0)=1/2, so the repeated-sampling coverage is below the posterior mass 0.95.

citations.quote: Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function

For $\beta>0$ and $M>0$, the **Gaussian-sequence hyperrectangle** of smoothness index $\beta$ and radius $M$ is $$\Theta_\beta(M):= \left\{\theta\in\ell^2(\mathbb N_+,\mathbb R): \sup_{i\ge1}i^{1+2\beta}\theta_i^2\le M\right\}.$$

for every integer $N\ge N_0$, $$\sum_{i=N}^{\infty}\theta_i^2 \le L_0\sum_{i=N}^{\lfloor\rho N\rfloor}\theta_i^2.$$ Thus each tail's total squared mass is controlled by the mass in the finite block from $N$ through $\lfloor\rho N\rfloor$.

For every deterministic nonnegative inflation sequence for which there exist $K_L\in(0,\infty)$ and $j_0\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $j\ge j_0$, $$L_{n_j}\le K_L\sqrt M\,\rho_j^{(1+2p)/(8+8\beta+8p)}$$ one has $$P_{\theta_0}^{(n_j)}\{\theta_0\in\widehat C_{n_j}(L_{n_j})\}\longrightarrow0.$$

Then there is a finite inflation constant $L>0$, depending only on the fixed model and class parameters, such that $$\inf_{\substack{\theta_0\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)\\ \theta_{0,1}=0}} P_{\theta_0}^{(n)}\{\theta_0\in\widehat C_n(L)\} \longrightarrow1.$$

At $\widehat\alpha_n>0$, let $r_{n,\gamma}(\widehat\alpha_n)$ be the $1-\gamma$ quantile of the centered posterior $\ell^2$ norm and use the posterior mean given above. Define the empirical-Bayes set by $$\widehat C_n(L;x)= \begin{cases} \{\theta\in\ell^2: \|\theta-\widehat\theta_{n,\widehat\alpha_n(x)}(x)\|_2 \le Lr_{n,\gamma}(\widehat\alpha_n(x))\},& \widehat\alpha_n(x)>0,\\ \ell^2,&\widehat\alpha_n(x)=0. \end{cases}$$
At a fixed truth $\theta\in\Theta$, its frequentist coverage is $c_n(\theta):=P_{\theta,n}\{y:\theta\in C_n(y)\}$.

The recursion separates earlier gaps below N_j/rho_j and the next gap beyond i_j; for large j the polished-tail block lies inside the current zero gap while i_j>N'_j lies outside every gap with positive coordinate, so the tail is positive and the block sum is zero.
For fixed L>=1 choose K_L=L/sqrt(M); since rho_j^q>=1 for q=(1+2p)/(8+8 beta+8p)>0, the source inflation bound holds and its sparse-gap theorem gives coverage tending to zero along n_j.
The positive conservative-coverage theorem assumes the polished-tail condition, which this witness violates, so the two source results have distinct scopes.
